title: eShop file classifications

classifications.name: Identity Server & Token Trust
classifications.question: Can someone mint, steal or misuse a token that Ordering, Basket, Catalog and Webhooks will trust, or sign in as another buyer?

classifications.name: Buyer Data Ownership
classifications.question: Can one buyer read, change or act on another buyer's orders, basket or webhook subscriptions?

classifications.name: Buyer Card Data
classifications.question: Can a card number or CVV reach a log, a token, a database column or a message?

classifications.name: Checkout & Order Submission
classifications.question: Can checkout place an order at a price other than the catalog's, create it twice, or empty the basket for an order that was never placed?

classifications.name: Order Status Saga
classifications.question: Can an order get stuck, skip a step or move twice between Submitted, AwaitingValidation, StockConfirmed, Paid, Shipped and Cancelled across Ordering, Catalog, OrderProcessor and PaymentProcessor?

classifications.name: Catalog Items & Stock
classifications.question: Can stock be confirmed without units or decremented twice, can an anonymous caller change items and prices, or can a picture request read files outside Pics?

classifications.name: Event Bus & Outbox
classifications.question: Can an integration event on eshop_event_bus be lost, published without its transaction, or handled twice?

classifications.name: Shared Message & gRPC Contracts
classifications.question: Does every copy of this message, proto or catalog DTO still match its counterparts by class and property name, so RabbitMQ routes it and it deserialises?

classifications.name: Webhook Subscriptions & Delivery
classifications.question: Can a webhook go to the wrong subscriber or an internal address, leak its token, or be accepted by WebhookClient without a valid token?

classifications.name: Schemas & Startup Migrations
classifications.question: Will this change run an unsafe migration against a live database at startup, or break a schema another service reads directly?

classifications.name: AI Concierge & Semantic Search
classifications.question: What buyer data reaches OpenAI or Ollama, and is the model's output trusted to change the basket, render markup or rank the catalog?

classifications.name: Aspire Host & Service Defaults
classifications.question: Does this change what the Aspire app exposes, how services find and trust each other, or a default every service inherits?

classifications.name: MAUI Mobile Clients
classifications.question: Can the mobile apps send a token on the wrong request, trust the wrong server, or report an order that was never placed?

classifications.name: Build, Packages & CI
classifications.question: Does this change which packages, feeds, warnings or CI checks protect the build?

classifications.name: Storefront & App UI
classifications.question: Presentation only: Razor pages, XAML views and front-end scripts.

classifications.name: Test Suites
classifications.question: Unit, functional and Playwright end-to-end tests.

classifications.name: Static Assets, Docs & Leftovers
classifications.question: Pictures, fonts, vendored libraries, docs and unused leftovers: no review needed.

plan.why: IdentityServer signs every token with the committed tempkey.jwk, with key management off (Identity.API/Program.cs:29, :37), and every API accepts tokens issued for any audience (AuthenticationExtensions.cs:49); a wrong change to clients, claims, token validation or forwarding silently grants access.

Ordering takes the order's buyer from the request body (OrdersApi.cs:150) and returns any order to any signed-in user (OrdersApi.cs:86-99, OrderQueries.cs); Basket and Webhooks scope data by the `sub` claim alone (ServerCallContextIdentityExtensions.cs:7, WebHooksApi.cs), so one dropped filter exposes another buyer's data.

The CVV is issued as the card_security_number claim (ProfileService.cs:77) and stored as plaintext (ApplicationUser.cs:16); OrdersApi logs the whole request, card number and CVV included, when x-requestid is missing (OrdersApi.cs:143), and the CVV stays out of the database only because PaymentMethod._securityNumber is unmapped.

Ordering stores the UnitPrice the client sends (BasketItemExtensions.cs:20); WebApp never checks the order POST's status before deleting the basket (OrderingService.cs:25, BasketState.cs:116); IdentifiedCommandHandler swallows exceptions, so a failed order commits partial work and its retry reads as a duplicate (IdentifiedCommandHandler.cs:99-101).

Order.cs's status guards are the only protection against redelivered events, since inbound handlers send plain commands (Order.cs:109, :129, :152); OrderProcessor finds grace-period orders by raw SQL on 'Submitted' and swallows database errors (GracePeriodOrdersRepository.cs:36, :50); PaymentProcessor's outcome is one config flag (OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmedIntegrationEventHandler.cs:27).

Catalog's item POST, PUT and DELETE have no authorization (CatalogApi.cs:106-123); the paid handler decrements stock with no de-duplication and RemoveStock throws at zero for the whole order (OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEventHandler.cs:19-26, CatalogItem.cs:70-84); only the PhysicalFileProvider in Program.cs:7-9 keeps picture reads inside Pics.

The RabbitMQ consumer acks a message even when its handler throws (RabbitMQEventBus.cs:170-180) and drops any message containing 'throw-fake-exception' (:163); Catalog never retries outbox rows that failed to publish (CatalogIntegrationEventService.cs:28-31), so a lost event stalls an order with no error.

Subscriptions are chosen by type only, so every subscriber receives every buyer's paid and shipped orders (WebhooksRetriever.cs:15); outbound calls go to user-supplied URLs with no allow-list (GrantUrlTesterService.cs:21-28, WebhooksSender.cs:25); WebhookClient's token check reads a key nothing sets, so it always passes (WebhookEndpoints.cs:13, :18, :37).

Every service applies its migrations and seed at startup in every environment (MigrateDbContextExtensions.cs:65-66, :81), and OrderProcessor reads Ordering's tables with raw SQL (GracePeriodOrdersRepository.cs:33-37), so a schema or enum-conversion change silently stops the grace period.

The concierge's tools hand the buyer's email, phone and address claims to the model and let it change the basket (ChatState.cs:97-111), and model-supplied image URLs are rendered as raw markup, which gives a prompt injection a channel to exfiltrate data (MessageProcessor.cs:24, :30).

Forwarded headers are switched on for every project, so any client can spoof X-Forwarded-For and defeat Identity's localhost-only diagnostics check (eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:36); the mobile BFF routes and WebApp's anonymous YARP proxy to catalog-api decide which internal APIs are reachable without auth (WebApp/Program.cs:32).

One shared HttpClient has its DefaultRequestHeaders rewritten on every call, so concurrent requests can carry another call's bearer token or client credentials (RequestProvider.cs:116, :136, :151); OrderService returns silently without a token while the checkout clears the basket and reports success (OrderService.cs:32-35, CheckoutViewModel.cs:115-127).

NuGet vulnerability warnings NU1901-NU1904 are suppressed for the whole repository (Directory.Build.props:11), so a package bump with a known CVE builds clean; nuget.config's package source mapping is the only guard against dependency confusion (nuget.config:5-13).

defects.title: IdentityServer signing key is committed.
defects.detail: tempkey.jwk holds the RSA private key, is loaded by AddDeveloperSigningCredential and key management is off, so anyone with the repository can mint tokens every API trusts.

defects.title: Client secrets are hard-coded as "secret".
defects.detail: The webapp, maui and webhooksclient OIDC clients share a literal secret, repeated in the WebApp and WebhookClient.

defects.title: The CVV is issued as a token claim and stored as plaintext.
defects.detail: ProfileService adds card_security_number to the claims, which AlwaysIncludeUserClaimsInIdToken puts in ID tokens.

defects.title: Demo users with a known password are seeded in every environment.
defects.detail: alice and bob are created with Pass123$ and card data wherever Identity.API starts.

defects.title: APIs accept tokens issued for any audience.
defects.detail: ValidateAudience is false in the shared JWT setup, and HTTPS metadata is not required.

defects.title: An order can be placed as another buyer.
defects.detail: CreateOrderAsync takes the buyer's id from the request body rather than the token.

defects.title: Any signed-in user can read, cancel or ship any order.
defects.detail: GetOrderAsync, cancel and ship have no ownership or role check; a bare catch also turns database errors into 404.

defects.title: Card number and CVV are logged when x-requestid is missing.
defects.detail: The warning logs the whole CreateOrderRequest with {@IntegrationEvent}.

defects.title: IdentifiedCommandHandler swallows exceptions.
defects.detail: The transaction commits partial work, such as clearing the basket, and the retry is treated as a duplicate.

defects.title: Ordering trusts the unit price the client sends.
defects.detail: BasketItem UnitPrice is copied into the order, and Order.GetTotal ignores the discount.

defects.title: Cancelling for rejected stock raises no domain event.
defects.detail: SetCancelledStatusWhenStockIsRejected changes status without an event, so no cancelled integration event is published.

defects.title: A CVV of four digits is rejected.
defects.detail: CreateOrderCommandValidator requires exactly 3 characters, but Amex is seeded as card type 1.

defects.title: The grace-period poller hides database errors.
defects.detail: NpgsqlException is caught and an empty list returned, so orders stay Submitted with no error.

defects.title: Catalog item writes are anonymous.
defects.detail: POST, PUT and DELETE on items have no authorization, so anyone can change prices and stock.

defects.title: The RabbitMQ consumer acks failed messages, and a test hook drops messages.
defects.detail: Messages are acked even when the handler throws, and any message containing 'throw-fake-exception' is discarded.

defects.title: Catalog's failed outbox events are never retried.
defects.detail: A publish failure marks the row PublishedFailed and nothing in Catalog re-reads it.

defects.title: Stock validation confirms products it cannot find.
defects.detail: Unknown product ids are skipped, so an order of only unknown products is confirmed.

defects.title: Every webhook subscriber receives every buyer's orders.
defects.detail: Subscriptions are selected by type only, and the payload includes BuyerName.

defects.title: Webhook calls go to any user-supplied URL, and the token is logged.
defects.detail: GrantUrlTesterService and WebhooksSender call subscriber URLs with no host allow-list (SSRF) and log the shared token at Information.

defects.title: WebhookClient's token check always passes.
defects.detail: It reads a top-level ValidateToken key that nothing sets, and /check echoes any token back.

defects.title: The Webhooks migration doesn't match its snapshot.
defects.detail: Initial creates nullable DestUrl and UserId with no indexes, while the snapshot has them required and indexed.

defects.title: WebApp empties the basket even when the order failed, and sends a fixed test card.
defects.detail: OrderingService never checks the response status; BasketState always sends card 1111222233334444 / 111.

defects.title: The concierge renders model-supplied image URLs.
defects.detail: MessageProcessor turns image markdown from the model into raw markup.

defects.title: The mobile app shares auth headers across concurrent requests.
defects.detail: RequestProvider sets Authorization and x-requestid on the singleton HttpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders, and x-requestid values accumulate.

defects.title: Forwarded headers are trusted from any client.
defects.detail: ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED is set for every project, which defeats the localhost check on Identity diagnostics.

defects.title: NuGet vulnerability warnings are suppressed repository-wide.
defects.detail: NU1901-NU1904 are in NoWarn, marked as temporary.

defects.title: HybridApp is never built in CI.
defects.detail: PR validation builds eShop.Web.slnf, which leaves HybridApp out, so changes to WebAppComponents can break it unnoticed.

decisions: High means a developer must review an AI's change to the file, rather than leaving it to AI review. This is the recommended definition, taken without asking: the user chose no questions after setup in /initialize-brown-field.
Themes were not put to the user for review, for the same reason; they come from four read-only scans of the code, and every High was checked against the code.
intent/**, .agents/** and .claude/** are out of scope: Intent Architect metadata, module-written agent instructions and local agent tooling.
Copies of integration events, the basket proto and shared catalog DTOs are Medium, not High: they are shared contracts, and High is kept for silent, serious failures.

notes.title: What High means here
notes.body: A developer must review an AI's change to these files rather than leave it to AI review. Medium files get AI review first, with a developer looking where it matters.

notes.title: Defects are recorded, not fixed
notes.body: The scan found real defects (committed signing key, anonymous catalog writes, webhook fan-out to every subscriber and more). They raise the importance of the files involved and are listed below; fixing them is separate work.
